topics: SOC 2 Type II report availability and evidence
Trust center access and audit evidence process
SSO / SAML / SCIM and RBAC model
Audit logs retention and log export
Encryption at rest / in transit and KMS integration
transcript:
[00:00] Lena (AE): Hi everyone, thanks for joining, were gonna run through Redwood's SOC 2 and ISO posture, give you the reports and answer Qs. Uh Omar from our security engineering team will cover the technical bits.
[00:18] Priya (CISO): Great hi, Priya here, were evaluating inference providers for PHI-adjacent workloads, so main concerns are SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 coverage, audit evidence, and data residency.
[00:34] Omar (SE): Thanks Priya, quick agenda: reports and trust center access, controls mapping (how our controls map to SOC2/ISO), RBAC/SSO integrations, audit logs and retention, encryption/KMS, and deployment/residency options.
[00:51] Mark (Head Eng): Quick note, Samir will own technical follow-up, we also need a controls mapping spreadsheet for our compliance team.
[01:05] Omar: Absolutely, we'll share a mapping. Plea-- sorry, please note our trust center has read-only artifacts, SoA, policies, and redacted evidence on request.
[01:22] Priya: On evidence: can you provide the full SOC2 report and the testing procedures? Wed like to see how controls were tested. Also ISO 27001 SoA and scope.
[01:37] Lena: Yes, we can provide SOC 2 Type II PDF and ISO SoA. We usually provide the full report under NDA and grant trust center access for evidence troves.
[01:49] Samir: How does trust center access work? Is it a portal or do you send bundles?
[01:56] Omar: It's a portal, a read-only dashboard. We can provision org-level access to security@cascademed.com. Sensitive evidence is redacted; if you need deeper artifacts we do a short access request and sign an NDA.
[02:12] Priya: Ok thats fine. We also need a controls mapping showing Redwood control IDs -> SOC 2 CCs and ISO 27001 Annex A controls. Do you map to both?
[02:25] Omar: Yes, we maintain a controls matrix that maps Redwood policies and configs to SOC 2 common criteria and ISO annex controls. We'll share a spreadsheet with the mapping, control owner, evidence links.
[02:38] Mark: Good. Now for SSO: we use Okta SAML + SCIM for provisioning. Can you integrate with SCIM for groups and RBAC?
[02:48] Lena: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. Omar can talk through role model and what attributes we support.
[02:56] Omar: Our RBAC model: org -> teams -> roles. We support SCIM group sync and can map Okta groups to Redwood roles. Token rotation, session length, and admin separation are configurable. Some logs show user activity for compliance.
[03:14] Priya: Is there an audit trail for admin actions and key changes? We need to see when KMS keys are rotated or when someone changes RBAC.
[03:23] Omar: Yes, all admin-level changes and KMS operations are logged. We ship logs to an internal ELK and keep an audit export for 12 months by default, with configurable retention for enterprise. We can push logs to your SIEM via S3 or syslog.
[03:39] Samir: Do logs include request/response payloads? We cannot accept patient data in logs.
[03:45] Omar: We redact request/response payloads by default. We also support prefix/KV caching but you can opt out. For PHI you should use Private deployment with customer-managed networking and optional in-house KMS.
[03:58] Priya: Tell us more about KMS options. We need customer-managed keys (CMK) and key rotation policies.
[04:05] Omar: We support bring-your-own-key via AWS KMS or external HSM integrations. For Private deployments you manage the KMS and keys, and Redwood uses envelope encryption. For hosted we can use customer KMS through a broker flow or use Redwood-managed keys; the control mapping will show which controls cover key management.
[04:25] Mark: Data residency — can we pin inference to eu-west-1 only? We need processing to remain in EU for some workflows.
[04:33] Omar: Yes, we have region pinning and routing policies. For hosted customers we run regional clusters; for strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private to guarantee all artifacts and logs stay in region. We'll note the deployment recommendations in the spreadsheet.
[04:48] Priya: What about SOC 2 coverage of your subcontractors — e.g., cloud provider?
[04:54] Lena: Our SOC 2 includes vendor management and shared responsibility sections. We have AWS SOC reports and third-party attestations referenced in our trust center. We also provide a list of subservices and their compliance posture.
[05:07] Samir: On encryption in transit: do you terminate TLS at the regional edge only, and do you support mTLS between services?
[05:15] Omar: TLS everywhere, and mTLS internally between services in our private networks. You can request stricter network controls for Dedicated.
[05:24] Priya: For evidence: how are penetration test results shared? Are you doing annual pentests?
[05:30] Omar: Yes, annual pentests and code security scans. We publish a summary and provide detailed reports under NDA.
[05:37] Mark: Any limitations on log export frequency or retention when forwarding to our SIEM?
[05:43] Omar: We support near-real-time streaming and batch exports. By default retention is 12 months, enterprise options up to 7 years.
[05:52] Priya: Need to confirm on-customer-data deletion procedures: if we terminate service, what happens to training/usage data and cached prefixes?
[06:00] Omar: We have data retention and deletion policies documented. For hosted we delete customer cached data within 30 days of termination unless a retention agreement is in place. For Private/Dedicated customers, you control retention settings.
[06:12] Lena: Quick clarifying q, Priya: Are you expecting us to sign a standard DPA and execute an MoU for evidence access?
[06:19] Priya: Yes, DPA signed, and for deep artifacts we want NDA.
[06:24] Lena: Noted, we'll send our DPA template and instructions.
[06:28] Samir: Any mention of model artifacts or weights in SOC2 scope? We want to know if model caching stores any customer prompt/result pairs.
[06:36] Omar: We do prefix/KV caching for latency. By default, cached prefixes are tenant-scoped and not used for model training. We'll include explicit notes in mapping and evidence.
[06:48] Priya: Do you provide a controls mapping to healthcare frameworks like HITRUST or just SOC2/ISO?
[06:55] Omar: We map primarily to SOC2 and ISO 27001; we can provide a custom mapping to HITRUST or NIST 800-53 on request — may take a bit longer.
[07:06] Mark: Competitors question: how do you compare with running on OpenAI endpoints re: control and KMS?
[07:13] Lena: The main diff is deployment modes — Redwood supports Hosted, Dedicated, Private with customer-controlled KMS and networking; that gives you more control than a pure-hosted provider.
[07:25] Priya: Ok, next steps and concrete ask: SOC2 PDF, ISO SoA, controls mapping spreadsheet, provision trust center access, schedule technical deep dive.
[07:33] Lena: Well do that. Omar, anything to add?
[07:37] Omar: I will prepare the mapping and RBAC/SCIM docs; provide examples of audit log exports and an architecture diagram showing KMS envelope encryption. We'll also include notes on redaction and PHI handling.
[07:51] Priya: One last thing — can you confirm retention and deletion for encrypted blobs if we use your hosted KMS vs BYOK?
[07:59] Omar: Hosted KMS: Redwood manages keys and we can delete blobs per policy; BYOK: you control key destruction and we cannot decrypt once you revoke keys. We'll put that explicitly in the mapping doc.
[08:14] Lena: Great, well share materials by EOD tomorrow. Any other open items?
[08:20] Mark: No, thanks. Priya: Thanks everyone.
[08:24] Lena: Thanks, talk soon.
[45:00] Meeting ended.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "K V cache" for KV cache), speaker labels may be slightly off, and timestamps are approximate. Links shared: https://trust.redwood.com/cascade-access (provisioning link), SOC2 report will be attached in trust center.
